title: Binary Johnson cardinality bound
statement: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $d$ be an integer with $1 \le d$ and $2d \le n$. Suppose $C$ is a finite set of binary words of length $n$ such that any two distinct words of $C$ are at Hamming distance at least $d$, and every word of $C$ has Hamming weight at most $w$. If $w \le J_2(n,d)$, where $J_2(n,d) = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(n - \sqrt{n(n-2d)}\bigr)$ is the binary Johnson radius, then $\abs{C} \le 2n$.
hypotheses_covered: distinct words of C at Hamming distance ≥ d
every word of C has weight ≤ w
replaced:
Assume $n > 0$, $1 \le d$ and $2d \le n$. If $C$ is a finite set of binary words of
length $n$ whose distinct elements are at Hamming distance at least $d$, whose weights
are all at most $w$, and if $w \le J_2(n,d)$, then $\abs{C} \le 2n$.
